items.text: "Switch to non-IT" gets treated online like a single leap.
This is not only about hours.
"I fixed bugs for six years" does not transfer.
You teach a subject, a skill, or a professional exam curriculum, in a college, a training company, a coaching institute, or an edtech platform.
People who already get asked "can you explain this simply" at work, and enjoy that more than the technical work itself.

blocks.heading: Run This Before You Pick a Door

items.text: Before you commit money or time to any single door, run your situation through The four questions, your fit, your situation, the job market and AI-proofing, the same fit check that should sit under any real career decision, adapted here for a full exit out of IT.
Teaching a room full of confused students, sitting a competitive exam for a defined number of years, or chasing a first client are each genuinely hard in a different way than IT is hard.
A 26-year-old with no dependents can absorb a year of government-exam prep or a lean freelance start.

blocks.heading: Do Not Resign, Enrol in a Full-Time

items.text: Pick one door from the six above based on your honest answers to the four questions.
Start one small, real test on the side: a weekend teaching batch, an SSC or banking mock test under real time pressure, or one small freelance project.

blocks.heading: It Depends Entirely on the Lane

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: It depends entirely on the lane and your starting seniority. Entry-level government exam roles (SSC CGL, banking PO) commonly start in the Rs 6-11 LPA range regardless of your prior IT salary. Corporate training, L&D, and non-IT consulting roles can land close to your current pay if you can show a portfolio of delivered outcomes. Entrepreneurship and freelancing usually mean near-zero or unpredictable income for the first several months, sometimes longer. Build your decision around a real number, not a hope.

visuals.heading: Questions Before Choosing

items.text: Build or confirm an emergency fund covering at least 6-12 months of full household expenses before you resign for a door with an unpredictable early income (entrepreneurship, freelancing, exam prep with no fallback job).
If you are financing a course or exam-prep coaching with savings or a loan, write the actual monthly cost against your realistic post-switch income, not the best-case story from an advertisement.
Separate "I am changing fields" from "I am also taking on new financial risk", doing both fully at once multiplies your risk instead of just adding it.
Fewer dependents usually means you can absorb a lean freelance start, a full government-exam attempt, or a lateral HR move while you build proof.
Age limits for most competitive government exams are still comfortably open in this window, if that door genuinely fits you.
Mistakes here are the cheapest they will ever be, use that window deliberately rather than drifting through it.

blocks.heading: Year and a Lot of Money

items.text: Resigning first and figuring out the door second, with no tested income plan behind the exit.
Treating one government exam as the only fallback, without a realistic view of the roughly 0.1-0.2% success rate at the top of that ladder.
Chasing "teaching" or "consulting" purely because they sound calmer, without testing whether the actual daily work suits you.
Starting a business or freelance practice with no first client already lined up before quitting.
Collecting certifications for three different doors at once instead of testing one door properly first.
